declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, supports preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from successive proposals and counterproposals addressing disputed certification and merits issues, the delay to trial, class recovery, fees, and distribution safeguards. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were discussed together from the outset; fees were not first discussed after agreement on class relief. The opening proposal sought $32 million for the class and $5 million in separately paid fees and expenses. Defense countered with $24 million and $4 million, respectively. Subsequent proposals maintained the $4 million fee-and-expense amount while negotiating the class fund, ultimately reaching $26.25 million for the class and $4 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval.

The settlement requires automatic distribution without claim forms. Notice and administration costs will be deducted from the class fund and must be competitively bid, itemized, and reviewed by the Court. Their amount has not yet been reliably estimated, so the final net recovery cannot yet be stated. Payment implementation includes secure records review, reasonable tracing, alternative payment methods where necessary, and court-approved redistribution. Unused administration reserves and remaining distribution funds will remain for class relief without reversion to Brightline. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Any fees the Court declines to award will augment class relief rather than revert to Brightline. All plaintiffs’ counsel fee allocations must fit within the stated $4 million amount.

Counsel considers the settlement fair, reasonable, and adequate in light of the substantial cash relief, automatic distribution, absence of reversion, and litigation risks. The class fund represents approximately 41% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges, before notice and administration costs. Although the action survived dismissal, certification remains unresolved and presents a significant risk. Success on the merits is also uncertain, and trial would be approximately two to three years away. Settlement avoids those risks and delays without conditioning recovery on submission of a claim.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP and Ostrander Bell LLP have filed overlapping actions concerning the same class. Approval of this settlement would release the covered class claims and affect those actions. Counsel has agreed to consult promptly with related counsel concerning coordinated approval proceedings and to disclose the overlapping actions to the Court; counsel does not represent that those firms have consented. Hargrove Lane LLP has a financial interest in the fee award, which is its only compensation for this contingency matter. Independent judicial scrutiny of fees remains essential notwithstanding the negotiated amount.

Counsel requests preliminary approval and authorization of appropriate class notice, subject to the Court’s review of the settlement documentation, proposed notice and distribution plan, administration budget, release, and adequacy of representation. Final approval and any fee award remain for the Court after notice, an opportunity for objections, and the required Rule 23(e) review.
